pk.context: 100 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: Mostly renal excretion of unchanged drug and DPP-4 selectivity over DPP-8 and DPP-9 mark this first-in-class gliptin.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is about 87% and a high-fat meal has no effect. Only 38% is protein bound, and about 79% is excreted unchanged in the urine.
Supplied as a phosphate monohydrate salt of molecular weight 523.32, against 407.31 for the free base. Soluble in water and in N,N-dimethyl formamide.
Marketed under an NDA in strengths of 25, 50 and 100 mg.

No boxed warning; the only contraindication is a serious hypersensitivity reaction to the drug itself, such as anaphylaxis or angioedema. Hypoglycemia is more frequent when it is added to other agents.
An adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Slows the inactivation of incretin hormones such as GLP-1 and GIP by blocking the enzyme DPP-4, but does not inhibit DPP-8 or DPP-9.
The generic name begins with S and has eleven letters.
